rascal noun

also good-for-nothing, scamp, heel (slang), worthless fellow, worthless (of a person), scoundrel, villain, gallows-bird, rogue, shameless wretch

nēquam (indecl.)

good-for-nothing, rascal

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Other words

  • nihil hominis esse — be a good-for-nothing

    nihil with the partitive genitive hominis: “to be nothing of a man” · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.32.77: cum Sōcratēs Alcibiadī persuāsisset eum nihil hominis esse (Lewis & Short), s.v. homō; Traupman 99; Traupman 322

  • furcifer, furciferī m. — scoundrel, gallows-bird (literally one who carries the furca, the fork tied on a slave’s neck as a punishment)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 677b: Furcifer, etiam mē dēlūsistī?; Cic. Vat. 15: id tū tibi, furcifer, sūmēs (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx convīciī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic., Hor.)

  • verberō, verberōnis m. — scoundrel (one who deserves a flogging)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 284: Ain' vērō, verberō?; Cic. Att. 14.6.1 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx convīciī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

  • mastīgia, mastīgiae m. — scoundrel, whipping-post

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 361: adsūdāscis jam ex metū, mastīgia; Ter. Ad. 781: nōn manum abstinēs, mastīgia?

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Greek μαστιγίας, one who is always being whipped.

  • carnifex (carnufex), carnificis m. — villain, scoundrel (literally hangman)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 518: Carnufex, nōn ego tē nōvī?; Cic. Pis. 11 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx convīciī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic.)

  • propudium, propudiī n. — a shameless wretch (properly a shameful act)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 190b: Quid ais, propudium?; Cic. Phil. 14.8: propudium illud et portentum (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx convīciī: Plaut.; Cic.)

    From prō and pudet.

Examples

  • homō nēquam

    a heel, a rotterTraupman 327

  • nēquissimus homō

    a worthless fellowTraupman 409

  • Ain' vērō, verberō? Deōs esse tuī similīs putās?

    What’s that, you scoundrel? Do you think the gods are like you?Plaut. Amph. 284

  • Carnufex, nōn ego tē nōvī? Abīn' ē cōnspectū meō?

    You villain, don’t I know you? Get out of my sight, will you?Plaut. Amph. 518

  • Quid ais, propudium?

    What’s that you say, you shameless wretch?Plaut. Curc. 190b

See also naughty, cheeky.
